Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 74, verse 18–24:

﴿Indeed, he reflected and calculated﴾ That is, he reflected on what he would say, and he arranged in his own mind what he would say about the Qur'an, that is, he prepared his speech. It is narrated that al-Walid heard the Qur'an and was impressed by it, and he nearly embraced Islam. Then he entered upon Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (رضي الله عنه), and Abu Jahl reproached him and said to him: "Indeed, Quraysh have come to hate you for your closeness to the matter of Muhammad, and nothing will secure your standing with them except that you say something about the words of Muhammad that will please them." I say it is magic, and that it is the word of a human being, not sent down from Allah." ﴿So may he be destroyed, how he calculated!﴾ This is a curse upon him and a condemnation, and he repeated it for emphasis in condemning him and denouncing his state. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: It is possible that its meaning is the approval of his first inclination when the Qur'an impressed him, so that his saying "qutila" (may he be destroyed) is not meant as a curse upon him, but is like their saying: "May Allah destroy so-and-so, how brave he is!", meaning amazement at his condition and the magnification of his description. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is possible that it is praise of him in the manner of mockery, or a quotation of the saying of Quraysh, ridiculing them. ﴿Then he looked﴾ That is, he looked at what was said. ﴿Then he frowned and scowled﴾ Al-busur is the contraction of the face, and it is stronger than al-'abus (frowning). He did this out of envy of the Prophet (ﷺ), that is, he frowned in his face, peace and blessings be upon him, or he frowned when his devices were exhausted and he did not know what to say. ﴿Then he turned away﴾ That is, he turned away from Islam. ﴿"This is nothing but magic transmitted from others"﴾ That is, it is transmitted from those who came before.

﴿Kalla﴾ is a rebuke to the disbelievers for their disbelief. Al-Zamakhshari said: it is a denial that they should have any reminder (dhikra). ﴿Idh adbar﴾ means "when it turned back," that is, withdrew. It is also read as *dabar* without the alif, and the meaning is the same. It was said that the meaning is "the passing of the night and the day," that is, it came after them. ﴿Wal-subhi idha asfar﴾ means "and by the morning when it brightens," that is, when it shines. Al-Zamakhshari said: it is not the feminine of *rahin*, because *fa'il* in the sense of *maf'ul* is used equally for masculine and feminine. Rather, it means *rahn* (a pledge), that is, every soul is a pledge with God for its deeds. ﴿Illa ashab al-yamin﴾: that is, the people of happiness, for they have freed their necks by their righteous deeds, just as the pledgor redeems his pledge by paying the debt. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: the companions of the right are children, for they have no deeds by which they are held in pledge. Ibn 'Abbas said: they are the angels. ﴿Yatasa'aluna * 'ani al-mujrimin﴾: that is, some of them ask one another about the state of the criminals who are in the Fire. ﴿Ma salakakum fi saqar﴾ means "What brought you into the Fire?" This is an address to the criminals. It may be that the Muslims or the angels addressed them with it, and they answered with their words: ﴿We were not of those who prayed﴾ and what follows, meaning that this is what made their entry into the Fire necessary. He delayed mention of denying the Day of Judgment to magnify it, because it is the greatest of their crimes. ﴿Nakhudu﴾: *al-khawd* is excessive speech about what is not befitting, of falsehood and the like. ﴿Hatta atana al-yaqin﴾: according to the exegetes, *al-yaqin* is death. Ibn 'Atiyya said: the certainty they meant is what they used to deny in the world, which they will be certain of after death. ﴿Fa-ma tanfa'uhum shafa'atu al-shafi'in﴾: that is only because they are disbelievers, and the scholars unanimously agreed that no one intercedes for the disbelievers. The plural *al-shafi'in* is evidence of their multitude, as reported in the traditions: the angels, the prophets, the scholars, the martyrs, and the righteous will intercede.

Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 74, verse 49–56:

﴿So what is wrong with them that they turn away from the Reminder?﴾ He means the disbelievers of Quraysh. ﴿As though they were startled donkeys﴾ "Mustanfirah" with a fatha on the fa' means the one frightened into flight by terror; with a kasra it means the fleeing one. He likened the disbelievers to fleeing donkeys in their ignorance and their aversion to Islam, and he means wild donkeys. ﴿Fleeing from a lion﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: al-qaswarah are the archers. He also said it means the lion. It was said: it means the voices of people. It was said: it means strong men. It was said: it means the darkness at the beginning of the night. ﴿Rather, each one of them desires to be given scrolls spread out﴾. The meaning: each person among them hopes that a book from Allah be sent down to him. "Munashsharah" means "manshurah," not folded, i.e., fresh, as it was written and not yet folded. That is because they said to the Messenger (ﷺ): "We will not follow you until you bring each one of us a book from the heaven, containing: from the Lord of the worlds to so-and-so son of so-and-so, that we are commanded to follow you." ﴿No!﴾ a rebuke against what they desired. ﴿Rather, they do not fear the Hereafter﴾, i.e., this is the cause and reason for their turning away. ﴿No!﴾ an emphasis on the first rebuke, or a rebuke against their not fearing the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, it is a Reminder﴾: the pronoun refers to what preceded in speech, or to the Qur'an in its entirety. ﴿So whoever wills, remembers it﴾: the subject of "wills" is a pronoun referring to "whoever," and in this there is encouragement and enticement. It was also said: the subject is Allah, and then the act of the servant is restricted by the will of Allah. ﴿He is worthy of piety and worthy of forgiveness﴾, i.e., He is worthy to be feared because of the severity of His punishment, and He is worthy to forgive sins through His generosity, the vastness of His mercy, and His grace.
